compliance.seismic: Designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 3

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 1828.8 m (6000 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing; short term 5 to 93 percent
environmental.operating-temp: 0 C to 40 C (32 F to 104 F)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C (-40 F to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.timing: 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB connectors and a PTP Ethernet SFP port

performance.packet-buffer: deep buffer from hybrid memory cubes (HMC)
performance.throughput: 2.88 Tbps and 1 Bpps of forwarding capacity (Q5 ASICs); 144 x 10 GbE, 36 x 40 GbE or 12 x 100 GbE ports (Table 2)

physical.mounting: four-post rack kit in the box; spare kits EX4500-4PST-RMK
physical.weight: 24.5 kg (54 lb) with two AC supplies, two blanks and three fan modules fitted; 24.3 kg (53.6 lb) for the DC build (Table 30)

platform.asic: Q5 packet forwarding ASICs with hybrid memory cubes
platform.storage: two 25 GB SSDs (the hardware inventory text also names a 25 GB NAND flash drive)

power.psu-ac-input: 100 to 127 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC at 50 to 60 Hz, 9.5 A at 100-120 VAC (Table 21); each supply has one input
power.psu-dc-input: -48 to -60 VDC rated, -40 to -72 VDC operating range, 40 A maximum; a 40 A breaker is recommended
power.psu-redundancy: four bays, 2N recommended; one supply runs the 36Q at 110 VAC or 220 VAC

thermal.airflow: port-to-FRU (airflow out, front-to-back); three 80 W fan modules at 150 CFM each, and fans in the supplies
thermal.heat-dissipation: 1,911 BTU/hr typical and 2,730 BTU/hr maximum (Tables 21 and 25)

configs.description: The QFX10002-36Q as shipped (Table 1 and Table 30): two 1600 W AC supplies in the lower bays, covers on the two upper bays and three fan modules, all with port-to-FRU airflow.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The DC build QFX10002-36Q-DC (Table 1): two 1600 W DC supplies in the lower bays and covers on the upper. Mixing AC and DC supplies in one chassis is not supported.
configs.name: dc

configs.description: The spare chassis QFX10002-36Q-CHAS-S (Table 3). The guide lists the chassis, the fan module and the supplies as separate spares and does not say what a spare chassis ships with, so it is read as the chassis alone with every bay open (estimated). It takes either feed once supplies are fitted.
configs.name: s

gaps.note: The HPE PSNow datasheet a00150807enw was tried once and the transfer failed (HTTP/2 stream error), so no datasheet is cited and no figure comes from one.
gaps.wanted: the HPE PSNow QFX10002 datasheet, for the bundle part numbers

gaps.note: The 72Q studio photographs (qfx10002-72q-front-high and -rear-high, tried once each) returned an HTML 404 page, so the 72Q has no studio photograph. This 36Q is checked against its own photographs.

The text says the bays of the 36Q and 72Q are numbered horizontally from the top left to the bottom right (0 to 3), but Figure 5 prints the digits 0 and 1 beside the two lower bays of the 36Q, where the switch ships its supplies, and prints nothing beside the upper bays that carry blanks. The bays take the text's numbers, the printing follows the figure.
gaps.wanted: the supply numbers printed on a 36Q, or the CLI names of its supplies

gaps.note: The guide's four-post procedure names no ear distance in millimetres and draws the rails only in perspective (Figures 33 to 35), so no ears position is written, and the spare kit EX4500-4PST-RMK is left out of chassis.kits in this slice.
gaps.wanted: the rail drawing and ear distances, and the four-post kit as a kit contract

gaps.note: The two-hole protective grounding terminal is shown in perspective on a side panel in Figure 36 and no flat view places it, so it is not placed. The guide states the screws (10-32 UNF x 0.25 in.) and the lug (Panduit LCD6-14BH-L) but not the hole spacing.
gaps.wanted: a flat side elevation with the terminal, and its hole spacing

gaps.wanted: a D-sub 3W3 connector in the connector registry

gaps.note: The text under Figure 21 says "the LED below the port indicates status and link" for the console, but no figure draws such a lamp: below CON is the reset button (callout 3). No console lamp is placed.
gaps.wanted: a close-up of the management panel

gaps.note: Table 15 gives one link and activity lamp for the SFP management port and the guide does not say which of the two lamps above the cages belongs to which cage. Each is tied to the cage under it, left to left.
gaps.wanted: the lamp assignment of the two SFP ports

gaps.note: The guide lists in prose what each port takes (QSFP+, QSFP28, DAC, AOC and breakout cables) but no transceiver table, so the port groups declare no interface.
gaps.wanted: the QFX10002 transceiver list from the Hardware Compatibility Tool

gaps.note: Figure 5 draws a narrow vertical plate near the right edge below the ESD point, x 432 to 440 and y 47 to 65, that the guide does not name. It is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: the name of that plate (a serial number label?)

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port group qsfp - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Description and Table 17 - every QFX10002 has port-to-FRU airflow (airflow out, AFO, front-to-back): air enters through the vents of the port panel and leaves through the FRU panel. The guide lists no back-to-front fan module or supply, so the device has no airflow configuration. The module handles are gold in the guide's tables and orange in the photograph (the photograph wins; see the module contracts).

colour.note: Median of the bare front face in the 36Q photograph (#c4c5c7 at the left margin, #bebfc1 and #cfcfcf near the right). The rear chassis reads #75777a in the rear photograph. The fan faces and the supply handles read #ec640e and #f94e16 in the photograph.

drawing-vs-photo.note: sources-disagree, and the real device wins for everything printed. Figure 19 and Figure 21 print PWR, MAJ, STS and MIN with the word ALARM in a bracket, the SFP legends MGMT and ETH, and 10MHz; the 36Q photograph prints PWR, MJR, STA and MNR, the legends MGMT and PTP, and 10M, with no bracket and no ALARM. The guide's own text (Table 16) names the lamps PWR, STA, MJR and MIN. The silkscreen follows the photograph. The drawing puts a laser-radiation label as a white box with printed words at the left end of the vent field; the photograph shows it yellow, so the plate is drawn yellow and its words, which cannot be read at this resolution, are not drawn.

envelope.note: Table 30, Physical Specifications for the QFX10002: 3.46 in. (8.8 cm) high, 17.36 in. (44.1 cm) wide, 31 in. (78.7 cm) deep "without handles for fans or power supplies". The height is carried as 88.0 mm, the 8.8 cm of the table (3.46 in. is 87.9 mm), 2RU. The face is the body between the folds with no ears drawn. The installation text gives 19 in. (48.26 cm) over the front mounting brackets. The depth 787.0 mm is the 78.7 cm of the table. The table gives the 36Q 54 lb (24.5 kg) with its supplies and fans fitted, and 53.6 lb (24.3 kg) for the DC build. The install topic gives the 36Q 54 lb (24.5 kg) too and the 72Q the same figures as the table, so no weight disagrees.

gate-1.note: Both flat figures pass at low resolution. Figure 19 (g050400, 1505 x 602 px, embedded image extracted from the PDF) gives a frame 1469 px wide (x 9.5 to 1478.5) and 293.5 px tall (y 149.5 to 443.0), aspect 5.005 against the stated 441.0 / 88.0 = 5.011, 0.1 percent out. Scaled on the width it is 3.331 px per mm across and 3.335 down. The cage pitch then reads 19.0 mm over the groups, the 19.0 mm of the QSFP ganged registry entry, a quantity the scale never saw. Figure 5 (g050404, rear, body 1464 x 294 px) is 0.7 percent out the other way, 3.320 px per mm across and 3.341 down. Positions are taken per axis on those scales and read to about half a millimetre.

gold-strip.note: Under the lower row the photograph shows a row of gold-coloured hexagonal dots from the left edge to the end of the cage block (median colour #cab284 and #e1ca9e) over a row of black vent holes. Figure 19 draws plain hexagon holes there. It is drawn as a gold band 2.6 mm tall at 78.6 mm down, estimated from the photograph, and is not drawn dot for dot.

grounding.note: Connect the QFX10002 to Ground and Figure 36 (g050389) - a two-hole protective grounding terminal on the chassis, for two 10-32 UNF x 0.25 in. screws and a Panduit LCD6-14BH-L lug. Figure 36 is a perspective view that shows it on a side panel, and no flat figure places it, so it is not modelled. See the gap grounding-terminal.

held-sources.note: The intake folder for the Juniper exqfx documents (COVERAGE.md, SOURCES.md and INVENTORY.md and its photographs) is under a path this account cannot read (permission denied), so the check for a held photograph, Visio stencil or 3D model could not be made. Only the public sources named above were used. If a held model exists it may refine the estimated positions.

hundred-gig-marks.note: Table 6 and the 100-Gbps text - "ports marked with a fine black line underneath the socket" take QSFP28 and run at 100 GbE, which disables the two neighbours (Table 7 - port 1 disables 0 and 2, port 5 disables 3 and 4, port 7 disables 6 and 8, and so on). The line is drawn under the lower cage of the first and third column of each group, ports 1, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 25, 29, 31 and 35 (12 ports, as the table says). Figure 19 draws a "100G" legend at the left end of the row and the photograph prints neither the legend nor a visible line at 4 px per mm, so the legend is not drawn and the lines are drawn thin, as the text says and the drawing shows.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-22. Juniper's own end-of-life pages (support.juniper.net/support/eol) were not read. An aggregator (router-switch.com EOL checker, QFX10002-36Q and -72Q) lists an end-of-life announcement of 2025-07-15, end of sale of 2026-01-15 and end of service life of 2031-01-15. It is not the maker, and the dates are carried as announced and flagged as unverified against Juniper.

logo.note: The maker's logo at the top right is not drawn. It is reserved as the region logo-zone, 22.0 x 8.4 mm, read off the photograph (the logo spans 409.5 to 434.2 across and 1.3 to 7.4 down). The model name below it is plain text and is drawn.

mgmt-panel.note: Figure 21 (g050373) callouts 1 to 9 and Figure 19, measured on Figure 19 per axis. Callout 1 is the em0 RJ-45 (1000BASE-T) management port centred at 392.4, 54.1; callout 2 the RJ-45 console (CON) at 412.1, 53.9; callout 3 the reset button, a round recess at 412.0, 63.2 below the console; callout 4 the four status lamps at 424.9 and 430.0 across and 51.9 and 56.9 down; callout 5 the em1 SFP management port (MGMT) at 380.4 across and 68.0 down; callout 6 the PTP Ethernet SFP port (the drawing labels it ETH, the photograph PTP) right of it at 395.4; callout 7 the PPS SMB at 414.2, 72.5; callout 8 the 10 MHz SMB at 422.2, 72.5; callout 9 the USB port, upright, at 430.9, 70.9 with the USB symbol below it. Two small round lamps above the two SFP cages at 392.2 and 398.0 across and 65.1 down are the SFP port lamps (Table 15 - one link and activity lamp). The two cages are 14.25 mm wide on a 15.0 mm pitch. Jack sizes come from the registry; the drawing's housing outlines are not used for size.

mounting.note: Mounting a QFX10002 in a Rack and Table 45 - a four-post kit ships in the box (two front mounting rails, two rear mounting blades, 24 flathead screws) and spare kits are ordered as EX4500-4PST-RMK. The rails fit the sides of the chassis (Figure 34) and the front rails may be flush with either end of the switch. The rack must have its rails 28 to 31 in. (71.1 to 78.7 cm) apart front to back. The guide gives no ear distance in millimetres and no rail drawing that can be measured and says the chassis must be supported at all four corners, so no ear position and no kit is written. EX4500-4PST-RMK is not listed under chassis.kits here (it is a shared four-post kit and follows in a later slice). See the gap rack-mounting.

port-leds.note: Figure 17 and Table 13 - each QSFP+ port has one bicolour LED, "triangle shaped". The strip between the two cages of a column draws an up triangle at its left, four small slots and a down triangle at its right. The up triangle is the upper port's lamp and the down triangle the lower port's, as the triangles point at their ports and as the library's SFP+ stacks draw them. The lamp centres are 7.0 mm left and 7.4 mm right of the column centre in the drawing, which the drawing keeps unequal, and 65.1 mm down. The slots are drawn as a vent pattern and are not hole for hole. Table 13 gives the states: green steady is a link (all four sub-channels up when channelized), green blinking is activity, slow green is the beacon, amber steady is some but not all sub-channels up (Junos 15.1X53-D21 and CPLD 1.16 and later) and amber blinking is activity on some sub-channels.

port-numbering.note: Figure 19 prints 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 34 above the upper row (above the first column of each group and the last column) and 1, 7, 13, 19, 25, 31 and 35 below the lower row, so a column holds the even port above the odd one and the ports run left to right, 0 to 35. THE PHOTOGRAPH PRINTS FEWER NUMBERS THAN THE DRAWING. In qfx10002-36q-front-high a "1" is printed under the first lower cage and "34" and "35" at the right end, and nothing at 6, 7, 12, 13 and so on, at the place where the drawing prints them and where "1" is plainly legible. The photograph is the real device, so only 1, 34 and 35 are printed here. "0" is not seen in the photograph (the place above the first cage shows vent holes) and is not printed. Numbering starts at 0, as the guide's CLI examples count (port 0 to port 35). Interface names are not printed on the metal and the guide does not state them, so none is carried.

ports.note: Figure 19 and Figure 6, counted - 36 QSFP+ cages in two rows of 18 columns, in six groups of three columns, each group one six-port (6XQSFP+) cage, with a 5.65 mm gutter between groups (the 62.65 mm group step less three 19.0 mm columns), carrying a column of hexagonal vent holes. Cells sit on the registry's 19.0 mm ganged QSFP pitch. The first column's left edge is at 6.85 mm and the upper row at 52.3 mm, the lower at 68.3 mm (row step 16.0 mm, which leaves 6.4 mm between a cage's bottom edge and the next cage's top for the lamp strip). The 36Q photograph agrees to a millimetre or two on the first cage (5.4 mm from the left edge, within the photograph's own perspective). Counts confirmed by Table 6 and by the NetBox elevation.

power-supplies.note: Table 30 - the 36Q ships "3 fans and 2 AC power supplies installed, 2 blanks", and Figure 5 draws the two supplies in the LOWER bays and the covers in the upper. Tables 4 and 5 and the redundancy text give four bays for every model and number them across from the top left. The bays here are psu-0 and psu-1 on the upper row and psu-2 and psu-3 on the lower, so the 36Q's supplies are in psu-2 and psu-3. Figure 5 prints the power symbols and the digits 0 and 1 beside the LOWER bays only, and Figure 4 prints 0 to 3 beside the four of the 72Q. The guide's text and Figure 5 therefore disagree on whether the 36Q's lower bays are 2 and 3 or 0 and 1; the legends are printed as Figure 5 draws them and the bay ids follow the text. See the gap psu-bay-numbering. The 36Q AC build runs on one supply at 100 to 120 VAC or at 220 VAC and the DC build on one DC supply (Table 4). Mixing AC and DC supplies is not supported.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) turns the lower cage of a belly to belly pair by 180 degrees. It is not applied here, because both rows are drawn alike. In Figure 7 and Figure 19 the two cages of a column are drawn with the same face, the latch bar low in the opening, and the studio photograph shows the same: the dark module bar high and the silver latch low in both rows. The convention is an estimate and the photograph overturns it, so both rows carry no rotation. The lamp strip lies between the rows.

usb-and-slots.note: The guide names no USB revision (Figure 21 callout 9, "USB port"), and the photograph shows a black tongue, which is neither colour the library's skins carry, so the white USB 2.0 skin is used and no 3.0 is claimed. The four small slots between the two lamps of each column are drawn as one dark plate 9.3 x 2.8 mm (the drawing shows two rows of four), centred 0.3 mm right of the column centre.
